director_mandate_binding.note: This spec refines the Director's binding question into the smallest rigorous falsifiable measurement. It preserves the frozen claim, the five discovery channels, K=3, threshold 0.50 and the >=2-engine materiality rule, and it repairs two v1 (EXP-FRONTIER-37984242167) defects: (a) the empty/non-reproducible frame is replaced by a live-certified non-empty DEEP frame, and (b) the v1 pool contained TWO guaranteed page-level-sitemap engines and an unreachable host (www.gnu.org, OSError 101), which made the positive branch foregone and broke a measurement prerequisite. The rewritten pool contains exactly ONE page-level anchor and three coarse/index-less-or-index-only engines, so the >=2-engine boundary is genuinely at risk.

question: On the credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate frozen by EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378, over a frozen 4-engine pool of DEEP (shortest-path hop in {3,4,5,6}) state-carrying items (a page whose HTML contains >=1 named <input>/<select>), what fraction of those items is reachable in <=K=3 fresh-agent GETs (1 discovery GET + 1 item-page GET + 1 spare) via ANY of five frozen site-native discovery channels (ROBOTS_SITEMAP, SITEMAP_XML, ON_SITE_SEARCH, RSS_ATOM, JSON_LD) -- with preregistered materiality threshold 0.50 on >=2 distinct host engines deciding whether shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier (persistent path caching is not a core optimization target; effort moves to discovery and substrate expansion) versus fresh deep-instance acquisition remaining path-bound with a computable persistence break-even surface?
hypothesis: H1 (DISCOVERY_COLLAPSES_DEPTH): on >=2 distinct host engines, >=0.50 of admitted DEEP state items are reachable in <=K=3 GETs via at least one frozen site-native discovery channel, so shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier and path/procedure persistence is not the primary optimization target. H0 (DEPTH_REMAINS_BARRIER): on fewer than 2 engines does the per-engine reachable fraction reach 0.50, so even with site-native discovery fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence retains a depth-dependent amortization surface. The experiment does not presuppose which holds.

falsifier.denominator: 40 admitted DEEP state items across 4 distinct host engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine; exact URL list frozen in target_pool.admitted_items)
falsifier.positive_branch: Let E = number of host engines whose discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= 0.50. SUPPORTS iff E >= 2. Then shortest-path hop is NOT a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier; persistence of paths/procedures is not the primary optimization target.
falsifier.negative_branch: Let E = number of host engines whose discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= 0.50. FALSIFIES iff E <= 1 (E==0 strict; E==1 reported as the MIXED sub-case). Then even with site-native discovery fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound and persistence retains a computable depth-dependent amortization surface.
falsifier.per_channel_disclosure: Mandatory per-channel coverage (discovery_reachable_fraction_per_channel) with any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items listed explicitly rather than counted as a null.
falsifier.why_reachable: E is not fixed by the frozen frame. The pool deliberately contains exactly ONE engine whose content sitemap enumerates its admitted items (vitepress.dev, page-level), ONE engine that publishes no content sitemap for the seed subtree but DOES publish a static content search index (nix.dev mdBook searchindex.js), and TWO engines with neither a content sitemap for the seed subtree nor any static search index (doc.rust-lang.org mdBook, rust-lang.github.io GitHub-Pages mdBook). Therefore E is expected to be 1..2 and the materiality boundary E>=2 requires the NON-TRIVIAL ON_SITE_SEARCH static-index channel to enumerate the nix.dev admitted items AND the single page-level sitemap to cover the vitepress admitted items: both SUPPORTS (E>=2) and FALSIFIES/MIXED (E<=1) are live on the frozen denominator. The design deliberately does NOT include a second page-level engine (which would make E>=2 foregone) and does NOT include a per-item reachability witness (which would pre-prove the outcome).

B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.description: Frozen item-blind same-host document-order link-following BFS (RED arm of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378): the number of HTTP GET requests issued before an admitted item page is first fetched, and the hop depth.
B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS.identifiable: Computed on the SAME admitted item set by re-running the frozen BFS at EXECUTE; deterministic on a stable site.

B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.role: theoretical O(1) lower bound when the item URL is already known
B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY.description: One GET to the already-known item page URL (RACQ_URL of EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378).

B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.role: contextual (NOT a comparator in the primary decision)
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.description: Persisted shortest-path replay cost hop+1 measured in the parent on a single-engine mdBook pool. Recorded as inherited context only; it is explicitly NOT re-measured here and is not used to compute the primary metric.
B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT.identifiable: Analytically defined; labeled inherited context, never paired with this experiment's discovery metric.

positive_control.description: At least one frozen site-native discovery channel must be probeable and return parsable same-host URL content (a non-empty parsed same-host URL set) on at least one host in the frozen pool, verified live during DESIGN.
positive_control.pass_criterion: At least one of the five channels yields a 2xx response whose parsed same-host URL set is non-empty on at least one host; verified in pre_freeze_control_certificate.channel_liveness.
positive_control.aggregate_only_note: This control is INSTRUMENT liveness only and is reported AGGREGATELY. DESIGN deliberately does NOT compute, and the certificate deliberately does NOT contain, any per-item or per-engine reachability witness. A per-item witness (v1 PC_KNOWN_DEEP_ITEM_WITNESS_BOUNDED) was REMOVED because it pre-computed which engines cross threshold and thereby made E foregone; the confirmatory per-engine fractions are measured only at EXECUTE.
positive_control.observed_pre_freeze: ROBOTS_SITEMAP and SITEMAP_XML returned non-empty parsed same-host URL sets on all four hosts; ON_SITE_SEARCH returned a non-empty parsed URL set on nix.dev (mdBook searchindex.js). For the two index-less hosts the channel sets returned no URL covering the seed subtree (doc.rust-lang.org's sitemap.txt is only the 3 version roots; rust-lang.github.io returns nothing).

null_control.description: Per host, two synthetic identifiers that do not exist are probed through the sitemap channels and by direct item-page fetch. They must yield zero discovered URLs and 404 on the item page, across all hosts.
null_control.pass_criterion: For all hosts and channels: 0 synthetic URLs discovered AND every synthetic item page returns 404.
null_control.purpose: Validates the channels/parser do not manufacture false-positive reachability via stale entries, redirects or parser errors.

NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.expected: synthetic URLs absent from every parsed sitemap/search URL set on every host
NC_SYNTHETIC_SITEMAP_ABSENCE.pre_freeze_observed: absent on all 4 hosts (null_sitemap_hit all false)

NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.expected: every synthetic item page returns HTTP 404
NC_SYNTHETIC_PAGE_404.pre_freeze_observed: 404 on all 8 synthetic probes (2 per host x 4 hosts)

operational_definitions.substrate: HTTP GET only via Python stdlib urllib; TLS verified; frozen User-Agent 'SPIDER-research-frontier-38013774272/1.0'; timeout 12s; max response body 600000 bytes; redirects followed; no credentials, cookies, browser, Docker, model key or write verb.
operational_definitions.navigation_graph: Directed graph whose nodes are canonicalized same-host http(s) URLs and whose edges are static <a href> links parsed in document order; asset extensions excluded; JS-generated links are NOT edges (disclosed VN-V2).
operational_definitions.hop_distance: Graph shortest-path length in edges from the seed root (hop 0), measured by the frozen BFS (budget B=250, depth cap D=6, each URL fetched at most once).
operational_definitions.state_carrying_item: A page that contains >=1 named form control: <input> with non-empty name attribute OR <select> with non-empty name attribute. The item observable is the page URL; named_controls is recorded per item.
operational_definitions.DEEP: hop in {3,4,5,6} (inherited from the parent's DEEP band; state items at hop<=2 are outside the frame).
operational_definitions.canonicalization: item URL canonical form = final URL after redirects, fragment removed, query string removed, trailing slash removed, and a terminal '.html' or '.htm' suffix removed from the last path segment (so a search-index entry ending in .html matches the same item's extensionless URL). Channel outputs are canonicalized identically before matching. Section-index directory URLs may retain a trailing path segment; the '.'-vs-'/' equivalence is NOT applied.

channel_definitions.ROBOTS_SITEMAP: GET https://<host>/robots.txt; extract Sitemap: directive URLs; GET each sitemap (gzip-decoded if .gz); if a sitemapindex, recurse into up to 12 child sitemaps; union all <loc>/plain-text URL entries; match the item's canonical URL.
channel_definitions.SITEMAP_XML: GET https://<host>/sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml directly (same recursion/gzip rules) and match the item's canonical URL.
channel_definitions.ON_SITE_SEARCH: On the seed root, locate a static <form> with a search-like action/input name; construct action?param=<item last path segment>; GET results; match item URL. Additionally probe well-known STATIC search-index artifacts referenced from or well-known relative to the seed root and parse them WITHOUT EXECUTING JS: JSON indexes (/search/search_index.json, /search-index.json, /search.json, /pagefind/pagefind-entry.json) AND JS-wrapped static index data files whose payload is a literal JSON object/array (notably mdBook /searchindex.js containing a "doc_urls" array). Extract URL/document entries and match item canonical URLs. This static-'.js'-index extension is REQUIRED for two-sidedness: without it mdBook content pages that have no sitemap coverage are undiscoverable by construction, which would manufacture a floor (a v1 defect). Any executed-JS or remote query endpoint is NOT invoked (disclosed).
channel_definitions.RSS_ATOM: Find <link rel=alternate type=application/rss+xml|application/atom+xml> on the seed root; GET the feed; match item URLs from <item><link>, <entry><link href> or <guid>.
channel_definitions.JSON_LD: GET the seed root as a discovery hub and enumerate same-host URLs from all <script type=application/ld+json> blocks (url/@id/mainEntityOfPage/itemListElement). ANTI-TAUTOLOGY: the item page itself is NOT used as its own JSON-LD hub (a self-fetch implementation is rejected).

operational_definitions.channel_success_rule: A channel succeeds for an item iff the item's canonical URL is discovered from that channel's output AND the item page is fetched with a final 2xx within the remaining K GETs. Each 3xx redirect counts as 1 GET.
operational_definitions.union_rule: item_reachable_via_discovery = OR(channel_success over the 5 channels); each channel is probed independently per fresh episode (no cross-item caching).
operational_definitions.sampling_rule: Frozen frame = for each seed, run the frozen BFS once (budget 250, depth 6); admit text/html pages at hop in {3,4,5,6} with >=1 named control; within an engine admit up to 10 items in BFS fetch order (hop bands interleaved by discovery order, deeper bands represented where control-bearing items exist). Deterministic; the exact admitted URL list is frozen in target_pool.admitted_items (40 items, 10 per engine).
operational_definitions.temporal_drift: EXECUTE measures discovery on the exact frozen admitted item URLs and re-runs the frozen BFS only to record hop depth; an admitted URL that no longer resolves at EXECUTE is excluded with a recorded reason and its exclusion reported. Frame drift is a disclosed validity threat.

measurement_validity.VN-V1_substrate: Credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP; no browser, Docker, model key, credential, cookie or write verb. Identical to EXP-FRONTIER-37950626378.
measurement_validity.VN-V2_static_parser_only: HTML parsed with stdlib html.parser/regex. JS-rendered navigation and JS search are NOT followed, so JS-dependent discovery channels are missed and disclosed as representation loss. Static JS-wrapped index DATA files are parsed as text without executing JS (see ON_SITE_SEARCH).
measurement_validity.VN-V3_same_host: Only same-host static navigation defines hop; cross-host navigation is out of scope, which bounds the claim to same-host acquisition on this substrate class.
measurement_validity.VN-V4_frame_certificate: The DEEP state-item frame was certified live during DESIGN across 4 distinct host engines (40 items) and pinned inline in target_pool.admitted_items (hashed inside spec.json by the freezer).
measurement_validity.VN-V5_k_budget: K=3 includes redirects and item-page fetch; the budget is generous relative to the 1-2 GET sitemap/feed/search-index discovery cost.
measurement_validity.VN-V6_channel_independence: Channels are probed independently and reported separately; overlap (e.g., robots.txt -> sitemap) is disclosed and the union is not double-counted per item.
measurement_validity.VN-V7_no_token_cost: No tokenizer/latency/dollar model; GET requests and response-body bytes are the only cost bases; token fields are null.
measurement_validity.VN-V8_selection_bias: The frozen pool is a purposive sample of public documentation engines that pass the depth+control frame gate, not a random Web sample. The metric is explicitly conditional on these engines; generalization beyond the admitted pool is not claimed.
measurement_validity.VN-V9_bimodality_disclosure: Design-time reconnaissance established that per-engine site-native discovery is close to a deterministic function of whether the engine publishes a machine-readable content index (content sitemap or static search index): engines that publish one tend toward fraction ~1.0 and engines that do not tend toward 0.0. The pool is therefore deliberately composed as exactly ONE page-level-sitemap engine, ONE static-search-index engine, and TWO index-less engines, so that the >=2-engine boundary is genuinely at risk and is NOT guaranteed by a second trivially-covering engine. The known cost of this composition is reduced power to detect intermediate fractions; this is disclosed as the central validity threat.
measurement_validity.VN-V10_sitemap_recursion_cap: sitemapindex recursion is capped at 12 child sitemaps and URL parsing at 20000 URLs per host to bound bytes; a host exceeding the cap is recorded with the cap hit.
measurement_validity.VN-V11_temporal_drift: Live hosts can change between DESIGN and EXECUTE; the frozen URL list is measured as-is and drift is recorded rather than silently re-sampled.
measurement_validity.VN-V12_availability: If a seed host is unreachable at EXECUTE, that engine is recorded as unavailable (excluded from E with reason); network failure is never encoded as a scientific negative.
measurement_validity.VN-V13_cross_subtree_items: The doc.rust-lang.org seed (/book/) reaches sibling rust books (/cargo/, root) at hop>=3 via the shared top navigation; these are retained as legitimate same-host DEEP state items and their cross-subtree origin is disclosed. The rust-lang.github.io seed (/async-book/) similarly reaches sibling projects (/rfcs/, /wg-async/); disclosed.

decision_rule.primary_metric: discovery_reachable_fraction = count(admitted DEEP items with item_reachable_via_discovery=true) / count(admitted DEEP items)
decision_rule.engine_count_variable: E = number of host engines with discovery_reachable_fraction_per_engine >= threshold among engines that are available at EXECUTE

outcome_mapping.MIXED: E == 1 (sub-case of the negative/materiality boundary; reported distinctly for mechanism localization)
outcome_mapping.INCONCLUSIVE: admission gate fails (pool < 10 admitted DEEP items total or fewer than 2 engines with >= 3 admitted DEEP items available) or a pre-registered measurement-validity gate fails

decision_rule.materiality_boundary: The preregistered materiality boundary is E >= 2. SUPPORTS requires E >= 2; both MIXED (E==1) and FALSIFIES (E==0) belong to the negative branch (depth remains an acquisition barrier).

admission_gate.on_failure: status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID/INCONCLUSIVE with the exact shortfall; no scientific branch is reported.

decision_rule.per_channel_reporting: Mandatory per-channel coverage for all 5 channels, with any channel yielding zero admitted DEEP items listed explicitly.
decision_rule.controls_observed_rule: If PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_LIVENESS fails, or either null sub-control fires, the run is status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID and no branch is scored.

product_consequence_positive: If SUPPORTS (E>=2): shortest-path hop is not a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier where a machine-readable content index (content sitemap or static search index) exists; persistent path caches are not the primary optimization target for SPIDER memory; effort shifts to discovery-channel coverage, engine/index-artifact detection, hybrid discovery+traversal for uncovered engines, and substrate expansion. C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY's 'pay for novelty, not the whole task' thesis is supported for the acquisition phase when such an index is available.
product_consequence_negative: If FALSIFIES/MIXED (E<2): even with site-native discovery, fresh deep-instance acquisition remains path-bound on a material share of engines; persistence of paths/procedures retains a real depth-dependent amortization surface whose break-even can be computed from measured re-derivation cost; memory architecture should keep investing in persistence with freshness guards and delta repair, and Frontier should improve discovery recall or adopt hybrid strategies.

estimated_cost.http_gets_estimate: ~2200-2800 GETs total: hop-confirmation BFS 4x250=1000 + discovery probing 40 items x 5 channels x <=3 GETs (~600 worst case) + channel hub/feed/robots/search-index fetches (~40, incl. nix.dev searchindex.js ~1-3 MB) + null control 8.
estimated_cost.external_dependencies: Public HTTP endpoints only; no API keys, credentials or rate-limited APIs.

expected_information_gain: High and decision-changing. The experiment measures, on a live-certified multi-engine DEEP frame, whether site-native discovery collapses the depth cost that motivates SPIDER's persistence architecture. SUPPORTS redirects the program from path persistence to discovery/substrate expansion; FALSIFIES/MIXED validates persistence and yields a real break-even surface. Per-engine and per-channel reporting localizes the mechanism (sitemap granularity, static-index availability, feed coverage) rather than reporting a single average.

decision_rule_reachability.reason: Denominator is non-zero and fixed: 40 admitted DEEP state items across 4 engines (>=10 total, >=3 per engine), frozen inline in target_pool.admitted_items. The two-sided rule is computable and both materiality regions are live: the pool contains exactly one page-level-sitemap engine (vitepress.dev), one static-search-index engine (nix.dev) and two index-less engines (doc.rust-lang.org, rust-lang.github.io), so E is expected to be 1..2 and the E>=2 boundary is genuinely at risk rather than foregone. No per-item witness pre-computes the outcome.

measurement_prerequisites.reason: All prerequisites are satisfied and were executed live in DESIGN on the FINAL pool: credential-free GET-only stdlib substrate works; every seed host is reachable (400+ byte 2xx on each seed); the DEEP state-item frame passes the gate on 4 hosts (10 items each, 40 total); the 5 channels are fully defined including static .js search-index parsing; sitemap channels returned parsable URL sets; the null control was run. The v1 unreachable host www.gnu.org (OSError 101, Network is unreachable) is REMOVED and is not referenced anywhere in this spec.

baseline_identifiability.reason: The within-experiment baseline B_LINK_FOLLOWING_BFS (requests-to-first-reach and hop) and B_DIRECT_URL_REPLAY (=1) are computable on the SAME frozen admitted item set under the frozen policy. B_PERSISTED_PATH_REACQUISITION_CONTEXT is analytically defined and explicitly labeled inherited context, never paired with this experiment's discovery metric. Identifiers are stable for EXECUTE/AUDIT reuse.

control_sensitivity.reason: Controls are non-tautological and can fire in both directions. NC_SYNTHETIC_UNREACHABLE_ITEM fires if a channel manufactures false reachability (pre-freeze: 0 discovered, 404 on all 8 synthetic probes). PC_DISCOVERY_CHANNEL_LIVENESS fires if channels/parsers break (pre-freeze: non-empty parsed same-host URL sets on all four hosts for the sitemap channels, and on nix.dev for ON_SITE_SEARCH). Crucially, the channel set is discriminative on the pool rather than constant: two hosts return zero for every channel while two hosts return non-empty sets, and the per-item witness that would have pre-proved the outcome has been removed.

treatment_liveness.reason: The treatment (5-channel site-native discovery probing, including static .js search-index parsing) is executable on the frozen pool using the stdlib GET substrate with no browser/Docker/model key, and was actually exercised in DESIGN: ROBOTS_SITEMAP and SITEMAP_XML returned non-empty parsable URL sets on all 4 hosts and ON_SITE_SEARCH returned a non-empty URL set on nix.dev (mdBook searchindex.js parsed as text). No treatment arm is structurally incapable of becoming EXECUTABLE.

freeze_artifacts_bound.reason: No separate mutable local code/data/task-bank/fixture file exists at DESIGN time and none is created (DESIGN scope is spec.json and prereg.md only). The complete sampling frame (seed list + exact admitted DEEP item URLs) is materialized inline in spec.json#target_pool.admitted_items, and all channel/decision definitions are in prereg.md; the deterministic freezer records the SHA-256 of both files in freeze.json.hashes, so the frame and decision rule are identity-bound by the frozen packet. EXECUTE derives its implementation verbatim from the frozen prereg and must publish its code + raw logs as result artifacts; no unbound mutable artifact can change the interpretation of the frozen decision rule.

target_pool.description: Frozen multi-engine DEEP state-item frame, certified live during DESIGN. Seeds, per-engine counts and the exact admitted item URL list are frozen here.

pre_freeze_control_certificate.policy_under_test: the frozen BFS + the 5 channel definitions in operational_definitions.channel_definitions
pre_freeze_control_certificate.note: The certificate proves (a) the DEEP state-item frame gate passes on 4 reachable hosts, (b) at least one discovery channel returns a non-empty parsable same-host URL set on at least one host, and (c) synthetic items are absent/404. It deliberately does NOT compute any per-item or per-engine reachability witness, and does NOT compute the aggregate discovery_reachable_fraction, which is the confirmatory measurement.
